subject: HSM onboarding: implementation fee offsets and credit scenarios
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ryan Cole <ryan@medvista.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HSM onboarding: implementation fee offsets and credit scenarios

Hi Ryan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I pulled together two concrete packaging options for the HSM/KMS onboarding and the related audit log retention work so you can take them into procurement/legal. High level: we want to keep the baseline offering simple while giving a clear pathway to offset the one-time implementation work with committed credits.

Option A — Seat model (easier compliance mapping)
- HSM seats: $6,000/seat/year (covers key escrow, attestations, per-seat SLA)
- One-time onboarding implementation fee: $45k (project plan, key import, attestation)
- Credit offset: we will apply up to $30k worth of credits tied to a 12-month committed usage = 18% effective offset if you sign 12-month commit at the below volume tiers.

Option B — Throughput model (simpler for your central infra team)
- HSM throughput add-on: +0.8c/1000 tokens processed on HSM-backed runs
- One-time onboarding fee: $35k (reduced because fewer seat-specific ops)
- Credit offset: up to $20k applied across first 9 months for a 9-month pilot commit

Deliverables and evidence — we will provide an Evidence Delivery Plan that lays out the attestation artifacts, audit-log samples, and handoff dates. I attached the onboarding workbook with the milestones and a short table showing how credits amortize against invoice schedule.

Ask: could you confirm which path procurement prefers (seat vs throughput) and whether they will accept amortization of credits across 6–12 months? If MedVista prefers, we can also propose a blended path (1 HSM seat + throughput uplift) to reduce overall $/seat.

I'll loop in Ben from finance for the final discount mechanics and Karthik for any technical clarifications.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: HSM_Onboarding_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), Evidence_Delivery_TOC.pdf (doc)

From: Ryan Cole <ryan@medvista.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medvista.com>, Aimee Lang <aimee.lang@medvista.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HSM onboarding: implementation fee offsets and credit scenarios

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the options. A few quick notes from procurement and legal:
- Procurement is inclined toward Option B (throughput) because we want fewer long-lived seat licenses to manage across regions.
- Legal asked for a clearer statement of what constitutes the "Evidence Delivery" and whether that can be tied to milestone-based credits rather than a single bulk credit. Aimee is copied for legal review.
- On amortization: procurement prefers credits applied over 9 months and an invoicing schedule that doesn’t front-load the full onboarding cost.

Two asks for clarity: can you provide a sample amortization schedule (monthly credit amount) and confirm whether the throughput uplift applies to all HSM-backed calls or only those routed through dedicated clusters?

Ryan
Director, Cloud Platforms
MedVista Health

Thanks Ryan — good directional feedback. Attached is a quick amortization CSV that maps both Option A and Option B over the time windows you suggested. Highlights:
- Option A (seat) amortized over 12 months: $45k impl fee with $30k credit => net $15k spread across first 3 invoices; or we can normalize across 12 months to smooth cashflow.
- Option B (throughput) amortized over 9 months: $35k impl fee with $20k credit => net $15k spread across 9 months (smaller monthly impact).

Technical note on routing: throughput uplift applies only to HSM-backed runs on dedicated clusters (we can route non-sensitive calls to cheaper variants). If you want the uplift to apply globally we'll need a routing rule which adds a small ops margin and changes the uplift by ~+0.15c/1000 tokens.

I've uploaded the amortization sheet to the shared drive (link below) and attached Impl_Fee_Amortization.csv to this thread. If procurement is comfortable with milestone-based credit releases (e.g., 50% on attestations, 50% on final evidence handoff) we can map those to invoices and the DocuSign SOW.

Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AbCdEfGhIJk/onboarding-workbook

Best,
Laura

Attachments: Impl_Fee_Amortization.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: HSM onboarding: implementation fee offsets and credit scenarios

Laura / Karthik —

Finance ok with amortizing the net implementation exposure, but a few guardrails from our side:
- The full credit stack requires a 9–12 month minimum commit; we can do 9 months only for Option B with a slightly lower max credit.
- If MedVista wants milestone-based credit releases, we need milestone acceptance criteria in the SOW (evidence checklist).
- Suggested commercial tweak: 12-month commit gets you the full credit amount + a 5% rebate on upstream token rates for the first 6 months. 9-month commit gets the smaller credit and no rebate.

Also, we should avoid a per-seat discount that scales below our published floor. Karthik, can you confirm whether a single hybrid seat + throughput model will materially change ops work?

Ben Carter
Sales Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Ryan Cole <ryan@medvista.com>, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM onboarding: implementation fee offsets and credit scenarios

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from the integrations side:
- Hybrid model (1 seat + throughput uplift) is feasible. Ops delta: additional key rotation automation and per-region attestations add ~10 engineer-days of work for the pilot plus extra runbook updates. That work is already captured in the $35k (Option B) and $45k (Option A) numbers, but if MedVista asks for multi-region attestations at Go-Live we'll need a small region surcharge (~$6k per additional region).
- Audit log retention: if you want >13 months retention in-region we need to provision disk and slightly higher ingest throughput; recommend a separate line item (we can show the cost as $0.02/GB/month or a fixed monthly retention fee).

Ryan — based on procurement's preference for throughput, we can propose Option B with: 9-month commit, $20k credit amortized monthly, milestone acceptance criteria in the SOW, and a DocuSign SOW that includes a Region Addendum clause. If that sounds good I can draft the technical appendix and hand it to Legal.

Karthik Iyer
Integrations Lead
Redwood Inference
